title: Grade 5 Science — Fri, Jun 05
description: The Skeletal System — Day 5 of 5: Synthesis — bones, joints, muscles and care
subject: science

questions.question: Put these in the correct order from largest framework to smallest unit: vertebra, skeleton, backbone.
questions.explanation: The skeleton contains the backbone, and the backbone is made of small vertebrae.

questions.question: The skull protects the brain and the rib cage protects the:
questions.explanation: The rib cage protects the heart and lungs.

questions.question: Which pair is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: The knee is a hinge joint; the shoulder is ball-and-socket and skull joints are fixed.

questions.question: Muscles move bones by pulling on them. Muscles are joined to bones by:
questions.explanation: Tendons attach muscles to bones; ligaments join bone to bone.

questions.question: When you straighten your bent arm, which muscle contracts?
questions.explanation: The triceps contracts to straighten the arm while the biceps relaxes.

questions.question: Which combination is needed to move your leg while walking?
questions.explanation: Movement needs muscles pulling bones at joints — all three work together.

questions.question: A friend twists her ankle and the ligaments are stretched. This injury is a:
questions.explanation: Stretching or tearing ligaments at a joint by twisting is a sprain.

questions.question: To keep bones strong, the BEST choice is to eat foods rich in calcium such as:
questions.explanation: Calcium from milk and leafy vegetables keeps bones strong.

questions.question: The heart muscle is different from arm muscles because it:
options: Works on its own all the time
questions.explanation: The heart is an involuntary muscle that works continuously without our control.

questions.question: Why does the backbone bend while the skull does not?
options: The backbone has many vertebrae with movable joints; the skull has fixed joints
The skull has muscles, the backbone does not
questions.explanation: Movable joints between vertebrae let the backbone bend; fixed joints lock the skull.

questions.question: Which is an example of an involuntary muscle?
questions.explanation: The stomach muscle works on its own and is an involuntary muscle.

questions.question: Sunlight helps our body because it helps make vitamin D, needed for:
questions.explanation: Vitamin D from sunlight helps the body use calcium for strong bones.

questions.question: Which action shows good care for your skeletal system?
questions.explanation: Good posture and regular exercise keep bones, joints and muscles healthy.

questions.question: If a bone breaks, what helps it heal in the right shape?
options: A plaster cast holding it still
questions.explanation: A plaster cast keeps the broken bone still so it can heal correctly.

questions.question: What is the MAIN reason the body needs a skeleton with joints and muscles?
options: To support the body, protect organs and allow movement
questions.explanation: Together they support and shape the body, protect organs and make movement possible.
